rules: When the topic goal, workspace, scope, and source-quality constraints are set and diverse perspective discovery can begin.
When the perspective map and source candidates are complete enough to guide grounded expert interviews.
When perspective discovery exposes a scope, source-access, or topic-definition decision that requires coordinator resolution.
When the interview transcripts, source-backed knowledge, and unresolved evidence limits are ready for outline synthesis.
When interviews reveal a missing viewpoint or evidence gap that requires another perspective search.
When the balanced hierarchical outline, section evidence map, and citation expectations are ready for article drafting.
When outline construction exposes an unsupported section or requires additional source-backed knowledge.
When the grounded long-form article is drafted with inline citations and is ready for final polish and verification.
When citation coverage, source linkage, duplication, or factual grounding requires article revision.
When the final article passes polish and citation verification and the coordinator needs the completed handoff and residual-risk report.
